Every coming is mentioned when truth flows into thought from the Word.

4713. "And the peace of the flock," which signifies how it stands with those who learn, or the Church, is evident from the signification of "peace," as how it behaves <note>regarding salvation and state</note>, mentioned just above in n. 4712; and from the signification of "flock," as those who learn. For the pastor or one who feeds is he who teaches and leads to the good of charity, and the flock is the one who learns and is led, as seen in n. 343; thus also the Church.

4714. "And bring back word to me," which signifies knowledge, is evident from the signification of "bringing back word," which is to report how the matter stands, thus knowledge.

4715. "And he sent him from the valley of Hebron," which signifies from the Divine Natural and Sensual, is evident from the signification of "being sent," which is to proceed and to teach, as seen above in n. 4710; from the signification of "valley," as those things which are below, as seen in n. 1723, 3417; and from the signification of "Hebron," as the Church of the Lord as to good, as seen in n. 2909. Thus by those words it is signified that He would teach those things which are lower in the Church; and this is because they could not grasp the higher things. For he who teaches faith and not charity can never perceive the higher or more interior things of the Church, for he has nothing that leads him, and which dictates whether this is of faith or whether this is true. But if he teaches charity, then he has good; this is his dictate and it leads him, for all truth is from good and acts concerning good—or what is the same, everything of faith is from charity and acts concerning charity. That everything of doctrine regards the life, anyone can know from natural light alone. 

That the Divine Natural and Sensual are signified by those words is a higher sense; for the lower things of the Church are said to be from the Divine Natural and Sensual of the Lord. This is not because these are lower in the Lord—for in the Lord and in His Divine Human everything is Infinite, for He is <term>Jehovah</term> as to both Essences, n. 2156, 2329, 2921, 3023—but because it is so with man. For those who are sensual men perceive those things which are in the Lord and from the Lord sensually, and those who are natural men perceive them naturally. It is spoken of in this way according to the quality of those who receive. Those, however, who are celestial men, and thus truly rational, perceive interior things; it is said of them that they are taught from the Divine Rational of the Lord. This is the higher sense, as stated, which is signified by those words. 

That "valleys" are the lower things of the Church can be established from other places in the Word; as in Isaiah: *“The prophecy of the valley of vision; what is it to you here, that you have all gone up to the rooftops? A day of tumult, and of treading down, and of perplexity to the Lord Jehovih Zebaoth, in the Valley of vision,”* XXII: 1, 5; the valley of vision stands for phantasies about spiritual things from sensual ones, thus from lower things. In the same: *“The choice of your valleys were filled with chariots, and the horsemen placed themselves at the gate,”* XXII: 7; the choice of valleys stands for goods and truths in the natural or external man. In the same: *“The voice of one crying in the wilderness, prepare the way of Jehovah, make straight in the desert a path for our God, every valley shall be exalted,”* XL: 3, 4; the valley stands for the humble.
